verdict.summary: Use one Dropbox OAuth app and connect each tenant's Dropbox account through that tenant's own authorization flow. Development is self-serve, but unrestricted production distribution requires Dropbox production approval; normally, Dropbox will not review the application until it has linked 50 users, unless it accepts an eligible early-review case. Prefer App folder access and progressive authorization unless the agent demonstrably needs files outside its dedicated folder.
verdict.activeEffort: 3–6 hours (estimate), mostly OAuth implementation, production-review materials, and tester coordination
verdict.waitTime: 2–5 business days after the 50-user eligibility gate (inferred from Dropbox's “few business days” response time) [inferred]; time to reach 50 linked users is unknown
verdict.mainGate: Unless Dropbox accepts an eligible early-review case, link at least 50 Dropbox users, then pass Dropbox's production-readiness review before unrestricted production distribution.

recommendation.text: Register one consumer Dropbox OAuth app for the product, have every tenant authorize their own account, start with App folder access, and request added scopes only when a user enables a feature that needs them. Escalate the shared-app architecture to API Support before production submission if the product resembles a platform exposing multiple independent third-party apps.

essentials.text: Use authorization-code OAuth with token_access_type=offline for background agent work. Treat access-token lifetime as the expiry returned by Dropbox; store refresh tokens encrypted and tenant-isolated, and refresh through /oauth2/token using grant_type=refresh_token. Refresh tokens can be reused and do not automatically expire, but can be revoked.

sources.quote: Dropbox access tokens are short lived, and will expire after a short period of time.
you’ll need to include token_access_type=offline as a parameter on your Authorization URL in order to return a refresh_token inside your access token payload.
The refresh token can be repeatedly re-used and doesn't expire automatically (though it can be revoked on demand).
To update your access token, call the /oauth2/token endpoint - specifying your refresh_token as a parameter and using the grant_type of refresh_token .

essentials.text: Register each exact HTTPS callback URI in the Developer Console and send the same redirect_uri in the authorization and token exchange flow. Dropbox rejects redirect targets that are not registered.

sources.quote: Redirection to any URI not specified here will not be allowed.
Dropbox checks that the specified redirect_uri parameter in your Authorization URL matches one of the registered values at authorization time.

detail.text: Draft a short reviewer script that demonstrates OAuth consent, the least-privilege boundary, an explicitly approved write action, and disconnect behavior. Supply this with a testable build if Dropbox requests production-review access.

steps.output:
Reviewer test script
1. Sign in with the supplied test account.
2. Open Settings → Dropbox → Connect.
3. Approve the displayed Dropbox permissions.
4. Ask the agent to list one file in its app folder.
5. Confirm it cannot access files outside that folder.
6. Enable write access, then approve creation of a test file.
7. Disconnect Dropbox and confirm later jobs stop.
